sources.entry: Pock - Display macOS Dock in Touch Bar.

summary.one_liner: Pock is a free, open-source macOS app that puts a widget bar into the MacBook Touch Bar, centered on a Dock widget that mirrors your Dock icons.
summary.what_it_does: Pock is a widgets manager for the MacBook Touch Bar. It ships with five default widgets: a Dock widget that shows your macOS Dock icons with badge support and multi-window support, a Now Playing widget with tap and swipe gestures for play/pause and track skipping, an ESC button, a Status widget for items such as time, WiFi and battery, and a Control Center widget for screen brightness and system volume sliders. A Weather widget shows the forecast for your location. Widget positions in the Touch Bar can be rearranged from a "Customize Pock" menu item, and preferences are accessed from the menu bar icon.
use_cases: Show the macOS Dock on the MacBook Touch Bar
Control media playback from the Touch Bar
Adjust screen brightness or volume from the Touch Bar
See time, WiFi or battery status on the Touch Bar
Check the weather on the Touch Bar
Build a custom Touch Bar widget with PockKit
how_to_run: Go to the official website and click download
Unzip the archive by double-clicking on the file or running `unzip`
Check the menu bar for the Pock icon to access preferences and widgets
If Pock does not appear in the Touch Bar, set Keyboard > "Touch Bar shows App Controls" in System Preferences and relaunch Pock
notable: Dock widget mirrors macOS Dock icons inside the Touch Bar, with badge and multi-window support
Five default widgets including Now Playing with gesture controls
Extensible through PockKit for building custom widgets
Free and open source under the MIT license
caveats: Only works on MacBooks with a Touch Bar
Sends anonymous usage/crash events over AppCenter; users who object are asked not to install it
Some translated READMEs may be incomplete
